clue.text: Risible as a footballer's mate

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as a pun: like a WAG, the tabloid label for a footballer's wife or girlfriend

explanation.walkthrough: WAG (wives and girlfriends) is British tabloid slang for footballers' partners, so a word ending -ISH can be read as 'like a WAG'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wag is a joker, so something waggish is humorous and laughable, which is what risible describes.

clue.text: Fixed poll (Labour leader excluded), or event showing state of anti-Corbyn MPs?

indicators.note: a fixed poll is rigged, so its letters and the others are rearranged
something excluded is kept out, so one letter of poll is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the opening letter of Labour is meant

parts.note: the opening letter of Labour, the one removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rigged ballot or some public event reveals how Labour MPs feel about Jeremy Corbyn, their leader.
explanation.walkthrough: POLL loses one L to leave POL, and those letters with OR EVENT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Open revolt is public rebellion, the condition Labour MPs hostile to Corbyn were in when they defied him in 2016.

clue.text: Our Theresa got round Gove's last illicit partner

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: had means got or obtained

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, taken from the name Gove

parts.note: the final letter of Gove
a mistress is a lover in an illicit affair

explanation.surface: Theresa May has dealt with Michael Gove's secret lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye's running parody casts Theresa May as the headmistress of a school, St Theresa's, writing newsletters to parents; E goes inside HAD to make HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Eye portrayed Prime Minister May as a school head writing to parents, so its readers know her by that title.

clue.text: Endless rubbish and mendacity — Tory and Labour style intimidation

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: bull is slang for nonsense
mendacity is telling lies

explanation.surface: A complaint that both main parties govern by nonsense, dishonesty and threats.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullying is the browbeating of the weaker, intimidation said here to be practised by both big parties.

clue.text: Sun victim: independent coach (American)

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for independent
a coach is a railway carriage, or car
US abbreviates the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A news-style item about someone hurt by the sun on an independently run American coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' wants to be a sports trainer or a bus; it is a railway car.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the wax of his wings melted when he flew too close to the sun, so he fell to his death.

clue.text: see 25ac.
Rubbish female (with piles) one married

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
piles and lots both mean a great quantity
a means one
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A rude dismissal of a married woman who has haemorrhoids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piles' wants to be the medical complaint; it means heaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is floating wreckage and, by extension, worthless discarded stuff, a synonym for junk.

clue.text: Drink epic julep to get pissed after one

indicators.note: being drunk leaves the letters staggering out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
a means one

explanation.surface: Advice to down a huge mint julep and get drunk after just one.
explanation.walkthrough: A julep is a bourbon and mint cocktail; the irony is that the answer is soft.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a beverage pressed from orchard fruit, so it is one example of something you take to quench thirst.

clue.text: see 18dn.
Encouragement to tennis player, having balls

parts.note: go! is a shout of encouragement
Rafael Nadal, the Spanish tennis champion

explanation.surface: Cheering on a tennis star who is holding the balls.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole first part reads as the cry 'Go, Nadal!'; 'balls' looks like tennis balls but means testicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Gonads are the sex glands, testicles in men, so gonadal means relating to or possessing them.

clue.text: Bride-like, about to give relief during rave?

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits inside it

parts.note: to rave is to talk wildly, to rant

indicators.note: turning about faces the other way, so the word for relief runs backwards

parts.note: aid and relief both mean help

explanation.surface: A wedding guest at a dance party, about to cool down a glowing bride.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock phrase 'a radiant bride' makes the glowing, happy look a byword for brides.

clue.text: Camp follower approached "right-on" casualty of Brexit

parts.note: the word that follows Camp in Camp David, the US presidential retreat
came means approached
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone trailing a camp approaches a trendy liberal hurt by Brexit.
explanation.walkthrough: A camp follower is normally a civilian trailing an army; here it is the word after Camp.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prime Minister who called the 2016 referendum resigned when Leave won, so the vote ended his career.

clue.text: Particulars of loud electronic component splitting re-formed Spice Girls at last

indicators.note: splitting a group means pushing in between its members
a band re-formed is put back together in a new shape, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
F is forte, the musical term for loud
IC is an integrated circuit

indicators.note: at the end means only the final letter of Girls is used

parts.note: the final letter of Girls

explanation.surface: Details of a noisy gadget that came between the members of the reunited Spice Girls.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged SPICE plus S are held apart by F and IC; the Spice Girls were a 1990s British pop group who re-formed in 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: Specifics are precise details or individual points, the same as particulars.

clue.text: Very old (dead?) Ford model — downfall of Putin's Russia?

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old
D is the abbreviation for dead
the Ka is a small Ford car

explanation.surface: A tired old Ford car is somehow linked to the collapse of Putin's state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downfall' suggests political collapse; it is used as one's undoing, like drink, and the question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy drinking of this spirit is a famous Russian weakness, so it is jokingly named as what will bring the country down.

clue.text: Wretched Donald's top — cor! right away reporter's down

indicators.note: the top of a name is its first letter, here of Donald

parts.note: the opening letter of Donald

indicators.note: sent away means removed, so cor and right leave the reporter word

parts.note: a correspondent is a journalist who reports
taken as written, the letters removed
R is the abbreviation for right, also removed

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a miserable Trump, with a journalist feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition appears at both ends of the clue; 'cor!' looks like a British exclamation of surprise but is just letters to strip out.
explanation.definitionFit: Despondent means dejected and low in spirits, which matches both the miserable and the fed-up senses given.

clue.text: Party takes Nigel's middle name, the cur's details

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, taken from Nigel

parts.note: the central letter of Nigel
a tag is a name or label

explanation.surface: A political party adopts Nigel Farage's middle name, giving away a scoundrel's personal information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nigel's middle name' reads as a quest for Farage's second name; it splits into the middle of Nigel and a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc on a pet's collar carries its owner's contact information, so a mongrel's particulars are on it.

clue.text: Bloody-minded bastards making a move, rejecting Theresa's lead, right?

indicators.note: letters that move shift position into a new order
what is rejected is thrown out, so the named letters leave the word

parts.note: taken as written
the first letter of Theresa, removed
R is the abbreviation for right, also removed

explanation.surface: Stubborn Tory rebels plot against Theresa May's leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: John Major called Eurosceptic rebels 'bastards'; BASTARDS without T and R leaves BASADS to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Badass is slang for tough and aggressively defiant, close to the obstinately awkward sense of the clue word.

clue.text: Cemetery bang in US police dept

parts.note: in American slang to bone, like to bang, is to have sex
the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's Metropolitan Police headquarters

explanation.surface: A graveyard where a shot rings out inside an American police department.
explanation.definitionFit: Boneyard is an informal word for a graveyard, where skeletons are buried.

clue.text: (& 9ac.) Tabloid hogwash, as manifested by Brexit vote

definitions.text: Tabloid hogwash, as manifested by Brexit vote

parts.note: surface reading: a sneer at the nonsense printed by the popular press
setter's reading: the phrase the tabloids used for the referendum result, which the setter dismisses as hogwash

explanation.walkthrough: After the 2016 referendum, pro-Leave papers insisted the result was a sacred popular mandate; the setter calls that phrase tabloid nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: The two words name the democratic wishes of the public, which pro-Brexit papers claimed the vote expressed.

clue.text: "Stephen shock" broadcast a number of occasions in the month

definitions.text: a number of occasions in the month

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard on air, so the words count by their sound

parts.note: Stephen Fry, the British comedian and broadcaster
to daze is to stun or shock

explanation.surface: A headline about a scandal involving Stephen Fry that is broadcast several times a month.
explanation.definitionFit: This weekday comes round four or five times in each calendar month.

clue.text: Cash machine points all round, giving instruction followed by Alice

indicators.note: points placed all round something surround it on both sides

parts.note: E for East, a compass point, used twice
an ATM is an automated teller machine

explanation.surface: A cash machine with directions all round it gives an instruction a woman named Alice obeys.
explanation.definitionFit: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, a cake labelled with these words makes Alice grow when she obeys it.

clue.text: To get in with someone is unfair? Vow to get screwed!

indicators.note: something screwed is twisted, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cynical aside that ingratiating oneself is unfair, followed by a promise to get bedded.
explanation.definitionFit: To win favour is to gain someone's approval, the same idiom as getting in with them.

clue.text: Bust-up about your out-of-date big shot

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the row word runs backwards

parts.note: a row is a quarrel
thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: A quarrel over your old-fashioned boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A worthy is a notable or important person, a dignitary, the same as a bigwig.

clue.text: Someone looking over super sexy Brenda

indicators.note: sexy letters are aroused and excited, so they shake into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A voyeur ogling a very attractive woman called Brenda.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called Queen Elizabeth II 'Brenda'.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read or examine something carefully, so a peruser is one who scans it.

clue.text: Head of bank having done a bunk, bear financial crisis

indicators.note: doing a bunk is running away, so that letter leaves

parts.note: Bruin is a traditional name for a bear

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, here of bank

parts.note: the opening letter of bank, removed

explanation.surface: A bank chief absconds, and a falling stock market brings a money disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' suggests a bear market; it is the animal. Doing a bunk is British slang for running off.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin is the loss of all one's money, the state of bankruptcy a financial collapse brings.

clue.text: Foregone conclusion of Hillary: that is, directed to absorb Democrat lead

indicators.note: absorbing something takes it inside
the conclusion of a word is its final letter, taken from Hillary

parts.note: the final letter of Hillary
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
led means directed
the first letter of Democrat

explanation.surface: Hillary Clinton's defeat was predictable: she had to take on the Democratic frontrunner role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foregone conclusion' looks like one phrase; the definition is only 'Foregone'. LED takes in D to make LDED.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo is to give up or surrender something, so foregone in that sense means relinquished.

clue.text: (& 6dn.) Leavers might need one, no longer getting sex by credit card

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so
it is slang for sex
Visa is a credit card brand

explanation.surface: Brexit voters who no longer have a sex life pay with plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leavers' looks like Brexit supporters; it means anyone departing a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Some states require this permit before a citizen may leave, so departing travellers might need one.

clue.text: A Corbyn hand book released about booze

something released is let go, so that letter is freed from the group

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book, removed
